Block ghost identities, composed density and the C50 lineage ledger

Use Canonical definitions and the canonical foundation. Symbols below are locally defined so that the block and C50 set notation cannot be confused with residual service-token counts.

Frozen labels and exact block definitions

In row ttt, every label <t<t<t is a frozen blocker, and every blocker p<tp<tp<t occurs exactly once at its persistent victim. To see the first direction, let rrr be a column's last recomputation before its first copied row. Recomputed value is at least rrr; COPY at r+1r+1r+1 requires it below r+1r+1r+1, so it equals rrr, making it the death blocker by the partition theorem. COPY then persists. Thus the number of frozen cells is A(t−1)A(t-1)A(t−1), not A(t)A(t)A(t).

An old diagonal label in row ttt is a ghost; its value is necessarily at least ttt, since diagonal labels cannot freeze. Let I(t)I(t)I(t) count all such row ghosts, Ht=#{a<t:d(a)>d(t)}H_t=\#\{a<t:d(a)>d(t)\}Ht​=#{a<t:d(a)>d(t)}, and bt=A(t)−A(t−1)b_t=A(t)-A(t-1)bt​=A(t)−A(t−1). The pool consists of row labels at least ttt that are not past diagonals and are not the current own diagonal. It includes blockers, including the death-row blocker ttt when present, and future diagonals. Write pool⁡(t)\operatorname{pool}(t)pool(t) for its size.

The overlap identity gives I(t)=2t+1−d(t)−HtI(t)=2t+1-d(t)-H_tI(t)=2t+1−d(t)−Ht​, hence G4(t)=I(t)−ygh⁡(t)G_4(t)=I(t)-\operatorname{ygh}(t)G4​(t)=I(t)−ygh(t). No ghost has value exactly t−1t-1t−1 in row t−1t-1t−1, because a prefix equality to the row index would make that label a blocker. Young counts below age 3 similarly include only existing nonnegative columns.

C50 sets, orbit roots and their exact counts

The injective map ddd has d(x)>xd(x)>xd(x)>x. Repeated inverse images strictly decrease integer indexes, so every nonnegative integer has a unique root: zero or a positive blocker. The forward orbit of a root is strictly increasing and unbounded, and these orbits partition the nonnegative integers.

For q≥1q\ge1q≥1, define owner sets

Pend⁡q={x<q:d(x)≥q},Hosted⁡q={x<q:d(x)∈Cq},Above⁡q={x<q:d(x)>d(q)}. \operatorname{Pend}_q=\{x<q:d(x)\ge q\},\quad \operatorname{Hosted}_q=\{x<q:d(x)\in C_q\},\quad \operatorname{Above}_q=\{x<q:d(x)>d(q)\}. Pendq​={x<q:d(x)≥q},Hostedq​={x<q:d(x)∈Cq​},Aboveq​={x<q:d(x)>d(q)}.

Here Cq={f(q,c):c<q}C_q=\{f(q,c):c<q\}Cq​={f(q,c):c<q} is the row prefix. Write Hq=Hosted⁡q⊔Above⁡q\mathcal H_q=\operatorname{Hosted}_q\sqcup\operatorname{Above}_qHq​=Hostedq​⊔Aboveq​; it is a set, not the scalar inversion count HqH_qHq​. An owner x∈Pend⁡qx\in\operatorname{Pend}_qx∈Pendq​ is absent when d(x)<d(q)d(x)<d(q)d(x)<d(q) and d(x)∉Cqd(x)\notin C_qd(x)∈/Cq​. Let AbsB⁡(q)\operatorname{AbsB}(q)AbsB(q) be the number absent.

∣Pend⁡q∣=1+A(q−1). |\operatorname{Pend}_q|=1+A(q-1). ∣Pendq​∣=1+A(q−1).

If a hosted diagonal were below qqq, it would be a frozen blocker, contradiction. Thus Hosted is contained in Pend; Above is also, since d(q)>qd(q)>qd(q)>q. Injectivity excludes d(x)=d(q)d(x)=d(q)d(x)=d(q) for x<qx<qx<q, and maximum makes hosted and above disjoint. These three classes partition Pend. Overlap gives

∣Hq∣=2q+1−d(q),AbsB⁡(q)=d(q)−2q+A(q−1). |\mathcal H_q|=2q+1-d(q),\qquad \operatorname{AbsB}(q)=d(q)-2q+A(q-1). ∣Hq​∣=2q+1−d(q),AbsB(q)=d(q)−2q+A(q−1).

One-row absence flux for a fixed root class

Fix a set CCC of roots once and for all. Let Abs⁡C(q)\operatorname{Abs}_C(q)AbsC​(q) count absent pending owners whose root lies in CCC. Among continuing owners x∈Pend⁡q∩Pend⁡q+1x\in\operatorname{Pend}_q\cap\operatorname{Pend}_{q+1}x∈Pendq​∩Pendq+1​, let FC+(q)F_C^+(q)FC+​(q) count not-absent to absent switches, and FC−(q)F_C^-(q)FC−​(q) absent to not-absent switches, always with root in CCC.

The entrant is x=qx=qx=q, because q<q+1≤d(q)q<q+1\le d(q)q<q+1≤d(q). Define

EC(q)=1[root⁡(q)∈C, d(q) absent at row q+1]. E_C(q)=1[\operatorname{root}(q)\in C,\ d(q)\text{ absent at row }q+1]. EC​(q)=1[root(q)∈C, d(q) absent at row q+1].

If qqq is a diagonal label, its unique owner xxx with d(x)=qd(x)=qd(x)=q exits Pend. This owner was absent at row qqq: the diagonal label qqq cannot occur at its numerical deadline in the prefix, and q<d(q)q<d(q)q<d(q). Define

Out⁡C(q)=1[q∈range⁡(d), root⁡(q)∈C]. \operatorname{Out}_C(q)=1[q\in\operatorname{range}(d),\ \operatorname{root}(q)\in C]. OutC​(q)=1[q∈range(d), root(q)∈C].

Its root agrees with that of its inverse owner. Since

Pend⁡q+1=(Pend⁡q∖{x:d(x)=q})∪{q}, \operatorname{Pend}_{q+1}=(\operatorname{Pend}_q\setminus\{x:d(x)=q\})\cup\{q\}, Pendq+1​=(Pendq​∖{x:d(x)=q})∪{q},

the exact change is the sum of continuing switches, entrant and exit:

Abs⁡C(q+1)−Abs⁡C(q)=FC+(q)−FC−(q)+EC(q)−Out⁡C(q). \operatorname{Abs}_C(q+1)-\operatorname{Abs}_C(q) =F_C^+(q)-F_C^-(q)+E_C(q)-\operatorname{Out}_C(q). AbsC​(q+1)−AbsC​(q)=FC+​(q)−FC−​(q)+EC​(q)−OutC​(q).

The formula is stated for q≥1q\ge1q≥1. With empty Pend at q=0q=0q=0, no exit and the entrant definition, it also extends to zero directly. Nothing bounds the flux difference asymptotically, and the root class cannot be changed after seeing each row.
